page: Microsoft Azure D48ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, translating to 4.0 GB of memory per core. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 2835 GB NVMe SSD and supports Premium Storage. There are no GPUs present on this server configuration.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities across multiple workloads. The Intel Xeon processor includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which contribute to strong performance in specialized tasks. In Geekbench testing, the server achieved a top-tier rating in image processing and strong results in software compilation and ray tracing. Memory bandwidth tests show strong performance for large block reads and writes, reaching 232.42 GB/sec and 100.8 GB/sec respectively. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Redis SET operations also register in the strong tier, with Redis handling 67.91 million operations per second.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and high-speed local NVMe storage, the D48ds_v6 offers a resource-dense profile suitable for database operations, web serving, and software development pipelines. Its qualitative cost efficiency is driven by the combination of dedicated compute resources, high-capacity local storage, and hardware-accelerated execution units like AMX, which enable efficient local LLM inference and data processing without requiring expensive GPU hardware. This makes it highly suitable for relational databases, Redis caching layers, static web serving, and enterprise applications.
